When the only thing you know about someone is their race, it makes sense to use your knowledge of their racial group to form an impression of them.
Law enforcement officers should pay particular attention to those social groups more heavily involved in crime, even if this means focusing on members of particular ethnic groups.

It is always wrong to avoid someone because members of their racial group are more likely to commit violent crimes.
Employers should consider an applicant's racial background when assessing their potential for leadership positions.
It's wrong to make assumptions about a neighborhood's quality of life based on its racial demographics.
